scenario: Data stored in tables with fixed columns and rows is best described as what?
explanation: Structured data follows a fixed schema of tables with rows and columns, as in relational databases. Semi-structured data (JSON, XML) has tags or keys but a flexible shape, and unstructured data (video, images, free text) has no schema.

refs.title: Explore core data concepts: Identify data formats

scenario: A JSON document where each item can have different fields is an example of what?
explanation: A JSON document is semi-structured: it has self-describing keys, but each item can have different fields. XML and YAML are other semi-structured formats. Structured data requires every row to share the same columns.

refs.title: Explore core data concepts: Identify data formats

scenario: Which is an example of unstructured data?

options.text: A CSV file of sales figures

explanation: Unstructured data has no predefined model or schema. Video, audio, images and free-form documents are classic examples. A table of orders is structured, and JSON or CSV data is structured or semi-structured.

refs.title: Explore core data concepts: Identify data formats

scenario: Which file format is columnar and optimized for analytics?
explanation: Parquet is a columnar format optimized for analytics: reading only the columns a query needs is fast and compresses well. ORC is also columnar. CSV, JSON and XML are text-based and row- or document-oriented.

refs.title: Explore core data concepts: Explore file storage

scenario: Which file format is a row-based binary format often used for streaming and serialization?
explanation: Avro is a row-based binary format often used for streaming and serialization, and it stores its schema as JSON alongside the binary data. Parquet and ORC are columnar, and CSV is plain text.

refs.title: Explore core data concepts: Explore file storage

scenario: Which workload handles many small, fast transactions like orders and payments?
explanation: OLTP workloads handle many small, fast transactions such as orders and payments. They are usually normalized and rely on ACID guarantees. OLAP is the opposite: complex reads over lots of historical data.

refs.title: Explore core data concepts: Explore transactional data processing

scenario: Which workload runs complex queries over large amounts of historical data for reporting?
explanation: OLAP (analytical processing) runs complex queries over large volumes of historical data for reporting and analysis. These systems are read-optimized and often denormalized, for example into star schemas. OLTP handles the day-to-day transactions.

refs.title: Explore core data concepts: Explore analytical data processing

scenario: What does ACID stand for in database transactions?
explanation: ACID stands for atomicity, consistency, isolation and durability, the guarantees that make database transactions reliable. Atomicity means a transaction either completes fully or not at all.

refs.title: Explore core data concepts: Explore transactional data processing

scenario: Which ACID property guarantees that a committed transaction survives a power failure?
explanation: Durability guarantees that once a transaction is committed, its changes are written to persistent storage and survive a crash or power failure. Atomicity is all-or-nothing, consistency keeps data valid, and isolation keeps concurrent transactions apart.

refs.title: Explore core data concepts: Explore transactional data processing

scenario: Which role is responsible for building pipelines that ingest and transform data?
explanation: Data engineers build and maintain the pipelines and storage that ingest, transform and integrate data. Data analysts explore and visualize it, and database administrators keep databases secure and available.

refs.title: Explore data roles and services: Explore job roles in the world of data

scenario: Which role is mainly responsible for backups, security and availability of databases?
explanation: Database administrators are responsible for backups, security, availability, patching and performance of databases. Data engineers build pipelines and analysts create reports.

refs.title: Explore data roles and services: Explore job roles in the world of data

scenario: Which role explores data and creates reports and visualizations to support decisions?
explanation: Data analysts explore data and build reports and visualizations, often in Power BI, to support business decisions. Engineers build pipelines and DBAs run the database platforms.

refs.title: Explore data roles and services: Explore job roles in the world of data

scenario: What is normalization in a relational database?

options.text: Splitting data into tables to reduce duplication
Combining all data into one wide table
Encrypting every column in every table
Copying the database to a second region

explanation: Normalization splits data into related tables, linked by keys, so each fact is stored once. That reduces duplication and improves consistency, which suits transactional systems. Combining everything into one wide table is the opposite (denormalization).

refs.title: Explore fundamental relational data concepts: Understand normalization

scenario: What is a primary key?

options.text: A column that uniquely identifies each row
A column that links to another table
An index created on every column of the table

explanation: A primary key uniquely identifies each row in a table, so it can't contain duplicates or nulls. A column that links to another table is a foreign key.

refs.title: Describe concepts of relational data: Explore relational data structures
Explore fundamental relational data concepts: Describe database objects

scenario: What is a foreign key?

options.text: A column that references a primary key in another table
A key stored in a database in another country
An encryption key used to protect backups
A unique key for every row

explanation: A foreign key is a column that references the primary key of another table, enforcing the relationship between the two. It need not be unique, so a customer ID can appear on many order rows.

refs.title: Describe concepts of relational data: Explore relational data structures
Explore fundamental relational data concepts: Describe database objects

scenario: Which SQL statement category includes CREATE, ALTER and DROP?
explanation: CREATE, ALTER and DROP are data definition language (DDL) statements that define database objects such as tables and views. DML (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, SELECT) works with the rows, and DCL (GRANT, REVOKE) manages permissions.

refs.title: Explore fundamental relational data concepts: Explore SQL
Transact-SQL statements

scenario: Which SQL statement category includes GRANT and REVOKE?
explanation: GRANT and REVOKE (and DENY) are data control language (DCL) statements that manage permissions on database objects. DDL defines objects and DML works with the data.

refs.title: Explore fundamental relational data concepts: Explore SQL
GRANT (Transact-SQL)

scenario: Which SQL statement adds new rows to a table?
explanation: INSERT adds new rows to a table. UPDATE changes existing rows, SELECT reads rows, and ALTER (a DDL statement) changes a table's structure. INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE and SELECT are the DML statements.

refs.title: Explore fundamental relational data concepts: Explore SQL
INSERT (Transact-SQL)

scenario: What is a view in a relational database?

options.text: A virtual table based on a query
A physical copy of a table stored on disk
options.note: Views store no data by default.

explanation: A view is a virtual table defined by a query. It stores no data of its own, which lets it simplify complex queries and limit which columns users can see.

refs.title: Explore fundamental relational data concepts: Describe database objects
Views

scenario: What is the main purpose of an index on a table?

options.text: Speed up queries that search or sort
Store a second copy of the table for backup

explanation: An index speeds up queries that search or sort on the indexed columns, much like a book index. The trade-off is that indexes add overhead to writes and take storage. Indexes don't encrypt data or enforce uniqueness unless declared unique.

refs.title: Explore fundamental relational data concepts: Describe database objects
Indexes

scenario: What is a stored procedure?

options.text: Saved SQL code that runs with parameters
A system table that stores error logs
A schedule for automatic database backups

explanation: A stored procedure is saved SQL code that you run by name, often with parameters. It encapsulates logic and can improve performance and security. It isn't a log, copy or backup schedule.

refs.title: Explore fundamental relational data concepts: Describe database objects
Stored Procedures (Database Engine)

scenario: Which processing type collects data over time and processes it in groups, like a nightly job?

options.note: Processes each event as it arrives.

explanation: Batch processing collects data over time and processes it in groups, like a nightly job. It is efficient for large volumes when low latency isn't needed. Stream processing handles data continuously as it arrives.

refs.title: Explore fundamentals of real-time analytics: Understand batch and stream processing

scenario: Which processing type handles sensor readings continuously as they arrive?
explanation: Stream processing handles data continuously as it arrives, which is what sensor readings need to power real-time dashboards and alerts. Batch processing would wait and process them in groups later.

refs.title: Explore fundamentals of real-time analytics: Understand batch and stream processing

scenario: In a star schema, which table stores numeric measures like sales amount?
explanation: In a star schema, the fact table holds numeric measures such as sales amount, and dimension tables hold the descriptive attributes used to filter and group them, such as product or date.

refs.title: Explore fundamentals of data visualization: Describe core concepts of data modeling
Explore core data concepts: Explore analytical data processing

scenario: Which data store keeps raw files of any format at low cost for later analysis?
explanation: A data lake stores raw files of any format (structured, semi-structured or unstructured) cheaply, for later analysis. A lakehouse adds warehouse-style querying on top of lake storage. A relational OLTP database requires a schema up front.

refs.title: Explore core data concepts: Explore databases
Explore Azure Storage for nonrelational data: Explore Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2

scenario: Which Azure SQL option is a fully managed PaaS database with no OS or instance to manage?
explanation: Azure SQL Database is a fully managed PaaS database engine: Azure handles patching, backups and high availability, and there is no OS or instance for you to manage. SQL Server on a VM is IaaS, and Table storage isn't a relational engine.

refs.title: Explore relational database services in Azure: Describe Azure SQL services and capabilities
What is the Azure SQL Database service?

scenario: A company needs near-100% compatibility with on-premises SQL Server, including SQL Agent, in a managed service. What fits?
explanation: Azure SQL Managed Instance offers near-100% compatibility with the latest SQL Server (Enterprise Edition) database engine, including features such as SQL Agent, as a managed PaaS service. That makes it ideal for lift-and-shift migrations with minimal changes. A single Azure SQL Database lacks instance-level features such as SQL Agent.

refs.title: What is Azure SQL Managed Instance?
Explore relational database services in Azure: Describe Azure SQL services and capabilities

scenario: A company needs full control of the OS and SQL Server configuration in Azure. What should it use?

options.text: SQL Server on Azure Virtual Machines

explanation: SQL Server on Azure Virtual Machines is IaaS: you get full control of the OS and SQL Server configuration, and you're responsible for patching and management. Azure SQL Database and Managed Instance hide the OS.

refs.title: Overview of SQL Server on Azure Windows Virtual Machines
Explore relational database services in Azure: Describe Azure SQL services and capabilities

scenario: Which Azure services offer managed open-source relational databases?

options.text: Azure Database for PostgreSQL and MySQL
Azure Cosmos DB for Apache Gremlin

explanation: Azure Database for PostgreSQL and Azure Database for MySQL are managed services for open-source relational databases, with Flexible Server as the main deployment option. Cosmos DB for Gremlin is a graph API, and Blob and Files are storage services.

refs.title: Explore relational database services in Azure: Describe Azure services for open-source databases
What is Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server?

scenario: Which Azure SQL Database purchasing model lets you choose compute and storage separately?
explanation: In the vCore-based purchasing model you choose the number of vCores, memory and storage independently. The DTU model bundles compute, memory and I/O into preset blocks. The vCore model also supports Azure Hybrid Benefit.

refs.title: vCore purchasing model
Purchasing Models

scenario: Which Azure SQL Database option automatically pauses when idle and bills per second of compute?
explanation: The serverless compute tier of Azure SQL Database scales compute automatically, bills per second for the compute used, and pauses the database when it's idle. It suits intermittent or unpredictable workloads. Elastic pools and Hyperscale don't pause databases.

refs.title: Serverless compute tier

scenario: Which option lets many Azure SQL databases share a pool of resources?
explanation: An elastic pool lets multiple databases share a pool of resources, which is cost-effective for SaaS apps with many databases whose load peaks at different times. Read replicas and failover groups are for scale-out reads and disaster recovery.

refs.title: Manage Multiple Databases with Elastic Pools

scenario: Which SQL query returns only customers from Ohio?

options.text: SELECT * FROM Customers ORDER BY State

explanation: The WHERE clause filters rows, so WHERE State = 'OH' returns only Ohio customers. ORDER BY only sorts, UPDATE changes data, and DELETE would remove the Ohio customers.

refs.title: Explore fundamental relational data concepts: Explore SQL
WHERE (Transact-SQL)

scenario: Which SQL clause combines rows from two tables based on a related column?
explanation: JOIN combines rows from two tables based on a related column. INNER JOIN returns only matching rows, while LEFT JOIN keeps all rows from the left table. GROUP BY aggregates, ORDER BY sorts and HAVING filters groups.

refs.title: Explore fundamental relational data concepts: Explore SQL
Joins (SQL Server)

scenario: Which SQL clause groups rows to compute totals per category?
explanation: GROUP BY groups rows so that aggregate functions such as SUM, COUNT and AVG compute a total per category. WHERE filters individual rows before grouping, and JOIN combines tables.

refs.title: Explore fundamental relational data concepts: Explore SQL
GROUP BY (Transact-SQL)

scenario: Which Azure SQL feature provides built-in high availability without extra configuration?

options.text: Automatic replicas managed by the service
Nightly exports of the data to Excel files
A single VM with no backups

explanation: Azure SQL Database includes built-in high availability: the service maintains replicas automatically with no configuration, and it offers a 99.99% SLA. Zone redundancy can add resilience against a datacenter failure. You don't set up log shipping yourself.

refs.title: Availability Through Local and Zone Redundancy
Explore relational database services in Azure: Describe Azure SQL services and capabilities

scenario: How long are automated backups kept by default for Azure SQL Database point-in-time restore?
explanation: Azure SQL Database takes automated backups and keeps them for point-in-time restore for 7 days by default, configurable from 1 to 35 days. Long-term retention can keep backups for up to 10 years. Backups are automatic.

refs.title: Automatic, Geo-Redundant Backups
Long-Term Retention Backups

scenario: Which feature encrypts Azure SQL Database data at rest by default?
explanation: Transparent data encryption (TDE) encrypts the database, backups and logs at rest, and it is on by default for new Azure SQL databases. Always Encrypted protects specific columns even from DBAs, and dynamic data masking only hides values in results.

refs.title: Transparent Data Encryption
Always Encrypted documentation

scenario: Which feature hides sensitive values like credit card numbers in query results for non-privileged users?
explanation: Dynamic data masking hides sensitive values, such as credit card numbers, in query results for non-privileged users. The stored data isn't changed, only what the query returns. TDE encrypts data at rest instead.

refs.title: Dynamic Data Masking

scenario: Which tool is a free, cross-platform app for querying Azure SQL and SQL Server?

options.text: VS Code with the mssql extension

options.note: Builds pipelines, not ad-hoc SQL queries.

explanation: Visual Studio Code with the mssql extension is a free, cross-platform tool (Windows, macOS, Linux) for querying Azure SQL and SQL Server. SSMS is Windows-only. Data Factory Studio and Storage Explorer don't run T-SQL queries.

refs.title: Quickstart: Run Your First Query
SQL Tools Overview

scenario: Which deployment model for Azure SQL Database scales storage up to 128 TB for very large databases?
explanation: Hyperscale separates compute from storage and supports very large databases, up to 128 TB, with fast scaling and quick backups and restores. Basic and Standard tiers have far lower size limits.

refs.title: What is the Hyperscale service tier?
Azure SQL Database Hyperscale FAQ

scenario: What's a benefit of PaaS databases like Azure SQL Database over SQL Server on a VM?

options.text: Ability to install any software on the server

explanation: PaaS databases such as Azure SQL Database reduce administration: Azure patches, backs up and maintains availability for you. The trade-off is less control, since you don't get OS-level access or the ability to install arbitrary software. Those are features of SQL Server on a VM.

refs.title: Explore relational database services in Azure: Describe Azure SQL services and capabilities
Describe concepts of relational data: Choose the right platform for a relational workload

scenario: Which relational database option should a company pick to migrate MariaDB workloads to Azure?

options.text: Azure Database for MySQL Flexible Server
Azure Cosmos DB for Apache Cassandra

explanation: Azure Database for MariaDB was retired, and Microsoft recommends migrating MariaDB workloads to Azure Database for MySQL Flexible Server because MariaDB and MySQL are closely related. Cosmos DB's Cassandra API and Managed Instance are different engines.

refs.title: Explore relational database services in Azure: Describe Azure services for open-source databases
What is Azure Database for MySQL flexible server?

scenario: Which object enforces that a column can't contain empty values?
explanation: A NOT NULL constraint prevents a column from holding empty (null) values. Other constraints include UNIQUE, CHECK, PRIMARY KEY and FOREIGN KEY. Views and stored procedures don't enforce column rules.

refs.title: Unique constraints and check constraints
Explore fundamental relational data concepts: Describe database objects

scenario: Which Azure feature lets a company use its existing SQL Server licenses to reduce Azure SQL costs?
explanation: Azure Hybrid Benefit lets you apply existing SQL Server licenses with Software Assurance to Azure SQL (vCore model) and SQL Server on Azure VMs, so you pay a reduced rate. Reservations, Spot VMs and Dev/Test pricing don't reuse existing licenses.

refs.title: Azure Hybrid Benefit
Explore relational database services in Azure: Describe Azure SQL services and capabilities

scenario: Which Azure SQL feature continuously copies a database to another region for disaster recovery?
explanation: Active geo-replication and auto-failover groups continuously copy a database to another region for disaster recovery. Failover groups add automatic failover and a single listener endpoint. Masking, elastic jobs and Query Store don't replicate data.

refs.title: Failover Groups Overview & Best Practices
Active Geo-Replication

scenario: Which Azure Storage service stores large amounts of unstructured objects like images and videos?
explanation: Azure Blob Storage stores massive amounts of unstructured object data, such as images and videos, in containers within a storage account. Files is for file shares, Table is key-value, and Queue is messaging.

refs.title: Explore Azure Storage for nonrelational data: Explore Azure blob storage
Introduction to Blob (object) Storage

scenario: Which Blob access tier has the lowest storage cost but requires hours to rehydrate data?
explanation: Archive is the lowest-cost tier for storage, but it is offline: you must rehydrate a blob to hot, cool or cold before you can read it, and rehydration can take hours. Hot, cool and cold are online tiers.

refs.title: Access tiers for blob data
Blob rehydration from the archive tier

scenario: Which feature turns Blob Storage into Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2?

options.text: Adding a private endpoint to the account

explanation: Enabling a hierarchical namespace on a storage account turns Blob Storage into Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2, adding real directories and POSIX-like permissions that analytics workloads need. Soft delete, tiers and private endpoints don't change the storage model.

refs.title: Explore Azure Storage for nonrelational data: Explore Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2
Azure Data Lake Storage overview

scenario: Which Azure service provides cloud file shares that can be mounted with SMB?
explanation: Azure Files provides fully managed cloud file shares that can be mounted using SMB (and NFS on premium accounts). Blob, Table and Cosmos DB aren't mountable file shares.

refs.title: Explore Azure Storage for nonrelational data: Explore Azure Files
What is Azure Files?

scenario: Which Azure Storage service stores key-value entities with a partition key and row key?
explanation: Azure Table storage stores NoSQL key-value entities identified by a partition key and a row key. Cosmos DB for Table offers the same API with better performance and global distribution.

refs.title: Explore Azure Storage for nonrelational data: Explore Azure Tables
Introduction to Table storage - Object storage in Azure

scenario: Which Azure database is globally distributed, multi-model NoSQL with single-digit millisecond latency?
explanation: Azure Cosmos DB is a fully managed, globally distributed, multi-model NoSQL database with single-digit millisecond latency. It can replicate to any Azure region and offers several consistency levels. Azure SQL and MySQL are relational, and Synapse is analytics.

refs.title: Explore fundamentals of Azure Cosmos DB: Describe Azure Cosmos DB
Azure Cosmos DB: Unified AI database

scenario: Which Azure Cosmos DB API stores JSON documents and is queried with a SQL-like language?
explanation: The API for NoSQL is Cosmos DB's native API. It stores JSON documents and is queried with a SQL-like language. Gremlin is for graphs, Cassandra for wide-column data and Table for key-value.

refs.title: Explore fundamentals of Azure Cosmos DB: Identify Azure Cosmos DB APIs

scenario: A company is moving a MongoDB app to Azure with minimal code changes. Which service fits?
explanation: Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB is wire-protocol compatible with MongoDB drivers, so a MongoDB app can move to Azure with minimal code changes. Azure SQL, PostgreSQL and Files are different data models.

refs.title: Explore fundamentals of Azure Cosmos DB: Identify Azure Cosmos DB APIs
Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB: Introduction and overview

scenario: Which Azure Cosmos DB API is best for data about relationships, like social networks?
explanation: The API for Apache Gremlin stores graph data as nodes (vertices) and relationships (edges), which fits data about relationships such as social networks. Table is key-value, MongoDB is document and Cassandra is wide-column.

refs.title: Explore fundamentals of Azure Cosmos DB: Identify Azure Cosmos DB APIs

scenario: Which Cosmos DB API suits apps already using Apache Cassandra's wide-column model?
explanation: The API for Apache Cassandra lets apps that already use Cassandra's wide-column model keep using CQL queries and drivers against Cosmos DB. Gremlin is graph, and the NoSQL API is the document model.

refs.title: Explore fundamentals of Azure Cosmos DB: Identify Azure Cosmos DB APIs

scenario: In Azure Cosmos DB, what does the partition key do?

options.text: Distributes data across physical partitions for scale
Encrypts each document with its own key
Sets the backup schedule for the container

explanation: The partition key distributes data across physical partitions so a container can scale horizontally. Choose a key with many distinct values so load is spread evenly. It doesn't control encryption, backups or permissions.

refs.title: Partitioning and horizontal scaling in Azure Cosmos DB
Partitioning and horizontal scaling in Azure Cosmos DB: Choose a partition key

scenario: Which unit measures throughput in Azure Cosmos DB?
explanation: Throughput in Azure Cosmos DB is measured in request units (RUs), a normalized cost of read, write and query operations. Throughput can be provisioned, autoscale or serverless. DTUs are an Azure SQL concept.

refs.title: Request Units as a throughput and performance currency in Azure Cosmos DB
Explore fundamentals of Azure Cosmos DB: Describe Azure Cosmos DB

scenario: What's the main trade-off when choosing a consistency level in Cosmos DB?

options.text: Stronger consistency means higher latency and lower availability
Weaker consistency always uses more storage space
Consistency settings only affect backup timing

explanation: Stronger consistency (such as strong) gives up some latency and availability, while weaker levels (session, consistent prefix, eventual) give better latency and availability. The five levels range from strong to bounded staleness, session, consistent prefix and eventual.

refs.title: Consistency level choices in Azure Cosmos DB
Explore fundamentals of Azure Cosmos DB: Describe Azure Cosmos DB

scenario: Which is a typical use case for non-relational databases?

options.text: Strictly normalized HR records with joins

explanation: Non-relational databases suit flexible schemas, high scale and low latency, for example a product catalog where each product has different attributes. Ledgers, strictly normalized HR data and multi-table joins are relational strengths.

refs.title: Describe concepts of relational data: Choose the right platform for a relational workload
Explore fundamentals of Azure Cosmos DB: Describe Azure Cosmos DB

scenario: Which Azure Storage redundancy option copies data to a secondary region?
explanation: Geo-redundant storage (GRS) copies data to a secondary region hundreds of miles away. LRS and ZRS stay within one region, and GZRS combines zone redundancy in the primary region with a secondary region.

refs.title: Data redundancy
Data redundancy: Redundancy in a secondary region

scenario: Which type of NoSQL database stores data as simple pairs for very fast lookups?
explanation: A key-value store keeps simple pairs of a unique key and a value, which makes lookups very fast. Azure Table storage and Cosmos DB for Table are key-value stores. Graph, column-family and relational stores model data differently.

refs.title: Explore fundamentals of Azure Cosmos DB: Identify Azure Cosmos DB APIs
Introduction to Table storage - Object storage in Azure

scenario: Which feature lets you recover accidentally deleted blobs within a retention period?
explanation: Soft delete retains deleted blobs for a retention period so you can restore them after accidental deletion. Versioning and point-in-time restore add more protection. The archive tier and hierarchical namespace don't provide recovery.

refs.title: Soft Delete for Blobs to Recover Data
Enable soft delete for blobs

scenario: What is Microsoft Fabric?

options.text: A unified analytics platform with a shared data lake (OneLake)
A relational database engine for OLTP apps
A virtual network service for hybrid connectivity

explanation: Microsoft Fabric is a unified analytics platform with a shared data lake, OneLake. It brings together Data Factory, Data Engineering, Data Warehouse, Real-Time Intelligence and Power BI in one product.

options.text: A single logical data lake for the whole organization
A backup vault for Azure virtual machines
A color theme for Power BI reports

scenario: Which Fabric item combines data lake files with tables you can query with SQL and Spark?
explanation: A lakehouse combines data lake files with tables you can query with SQL and Spark. In Fabric it stores data in Delta format in OneLake. An eventstream ingests streaming events and a Power BI dashboard visualizes.

scenario: Which open table format adds transactions and versioning to data lake files?
explanation: Delta Lake is an open table format that adds ACID transactions, versioning and time travel to Parquet files in a data lake. CSV, XML and ZIP files provide none of those.

Lakehouse and Delta Tables

scenario: Which service orchestrates data movement and transformation with pipelines and connectors?
explanation: Azure Data Factory orchestrates data movement and transformation with pipelines and connectors. Fabric Data Factory offers similar pipelines inside Fabric. Key Vault, Bastion and DNS aren't data integration services.

scenario: What is ETL?
explanation: ETL stands for extract, transform, load: data is extracted from sources, transformed in a separate engine, then loaded into the destination. ELT loads the raw data first and transforms it in the destination.

refs.title: Explore concepts of data analytics: Describe data ingestion and processing

scenario: Which service is an Apache Spark-based analytics platform for data engineering and data science?
explanation: Azure Databricks is an Apache Spark-based analytics platform for data engineering and data science. Spark also runs in Microsoft Fabric and Azure Synapse Analytics. Azure SQL Database, Files and Monitor aren't Spark platforms.

refs.title: What is Azure Databricks?

scenario: Which Microsoft tool creates interactive reports and dashboards from data models?
explanation: Power BI creates interactive reports and dashboards from data models. Power BI Desktop builds reports and the Power BI service shares them. Data Factory moves data, Event Hubs ingests events and Stream Analytics processes streams.

scenario: In Power BI, what's the difference between a report and a dashboard?

options.text: Reports have multiple interactive pages; dashboards are single-page pinned tiles
Dashboards can only be built in Excel, reports only in Power BI
Reports hold raw tables; dashboards hold the visuals

explanation: A report has one or more interactive pages of visuals built on a semantic model. A dashboard is a single page of tiles pinned from reports (and other sources) in the Power BI service. They aren't the same, and both are Power BI items.

scenario: Which Power BI visual is best for showing a trend over time?
explanation: A line chart is best for showing a trend over time because it connects values across a continuous axis. Bar or column charts compare categories, a card shows a single number and a pie chart shows proportions.

refs.title: Explore fundamentals of data visualization: Describe considerations for data visualization
Overview of visualizations in Power BI

scenario: Which service ingests millions of events per second from apps and devices?
explanation: Azure Event Hubs is a big-data streaming platform that ingests millions of events per second from apps and devices. It is often paired with Stream Analytics or Fabric Real-Time Intelligence to process them.

refs.title: What is Azure Event Hubs - Real-time data streaming platform
Explore fundamentals of real-time analytics: Explore common elements of stream processing architecture

scenario: Which service runs SQL-like queries on streaming data in real time?
explanation: Azure Stream Analytics runs SQL-like queries over streaming data in real time and supports windowing functions such as tumbling and hopping windows. Data Factory is for batch movement and Blob Storage just stores data.

refs.title: Introduction to Azure Stream Analytics
Azure Stream Analytics Windowing Functions Overview

scenario: Which Fabric experience handles streaming data with eventstreams and KQL databases?
explanation: Real-Time Intelligence in Fabric handles streaming data with eventstreams, and stores event data in eventhouses (KQL databases) queried with Kusto Query Language. Data Warehouse and Data Factory are for other workloads.

refs.title: Explore fundamentals of real-time analytics: Explore Microsoft Fabric Real-Time Intelligence
What Is Real-Time Intelligence in Microsoft Fabric?

scenario: What is a data warehouse?

options.text: A store of structured data optimized for analytical queries
A store of raw files in any format
A cache that stores frequently used web pages

explanation: A data warehouse is a store of structured data optimized for analytical queries, usually modeled as star or snowflake schemas. A data lake holds raw files, a cache holds hot content and an OLTP database handles transactions.

refs.title: Explore core data concepts: Explore databases
What Is Fabric Data Warehouse?

scenario: Which service provides an enterprise analytics platform combining SQL pools, Spark and pipelines in Azure?
explanation: Azure Synapse Analytics is an enterprise analytics platform combining SQL pools, Spark and pipelines. Microsoft Fabric is the newer unified platform for many of these workloads. Cosmos DB, PostgreSQL and Files aren't analytics platforms.

refs.title: What is Azure Synapse Analytics?

scenario: In data modeling for Power BI, what is a measure?

options.text: A calculation, like total sales, evaluated in context
A connection to an external data source

explanation: A measure is a calculation, such as total sales, that is evaluated in the context of the report's filters and visuals. Measures are written in DAX (Data Analysis Expressions).

refs.title: Explore fundamentals of data visualization: Describe core concepts of data modeling
DAX overview

scenario: Why is a star schema common in analytical models?

options.text: It simplifies queries and improves performance
It removes the need for any keys between tables

explanation: A star schema simplifies queries and improves performance for analytical models: facts link to dimension tables by keys, which makes filtering and aggregation fast. It still needs keys and holds structured data.

scenario: What's the main difference between batch and streaming analytics latency?

options.text: Streaming produces results in seconds; batch in minutes or hours
Batch always returns results faster than streaming

explanation: Streaming analytics produces results within seconds of data arriving, while batch analytics runs on accumulated data and returns results in minutes or hours. Many architectures combine both.

scenario: Which Fabric item supports T-SQL for reading and writing structured data with full transactional support?
explanation: A Fabric warehouse supports T-SQL for both reading and writing with full transactional support. A lakehouse's SQL analytics endpoint is read-only. Eventstreams, notebooks and semantic models do other jobs.

scenario: A team wants to clean and shape data visually with Power Query before loading it. What should they use?
explanation: Dataflows (Dataflows Gen2 in Fabric) use the Power Query low-code editor to clean and shape data visually before loading it. Event Hubs, Key Vault and Bastion don't transform data.

scenario: What is a semantic model in Power BI?

options.text: Tables, relationships and measures that reports are built on
A machine learning model trained on report data

explanation: A semantic model (formerly called a dataset) holds the tables, relationships and measures that Power BI reports are built on. It isn't a machine learning model, storage account type or security policy.

scenario: Which tool lets business users explore data with natural language questions in Power BI?
explanation: Copilot in Power BI (and Q&A) lets business users explore data by asking questions in natural language. Copilot can also draft report pages and summaries. Bastion, Data Factory and SQL Agent don't offer a natural-language interface.

scenario: What's the main purpose of data ingestion in an analytics solution?

options.text: Bringing data from sources into the analytics store

explanation: Data ingestion brings data from its sources into the analytics store. Transformation, modeling and visualization come after ingestion. It isn't about deleting, encrypting or securing data.

scenario: Which component of a modern data warehouse typically stores raw data before it's transformed?

options.text: A data lake (often the bronze layer)

explanation: Raw data lands in a data lake, often called the bronze layer in the medallion architecture, before it's cleaned (silver) and made business-ready (gold). A dashboard, semantic model or VPN gateway doesn't hold raw data.

scenario: A retail point-of-sale system records thousands of small sales a minute, each of which must be saved immediately and reliably. Which type of data workload is this?

options.note: OLAP serves large read-heavy queries for analysis, not many small writes.
Batch handles data in scheduled groups, not each sale as it happens.
Streaming analyzes events in motion; it isn't the system of record for transactions.

explanation: A point-of-sale system that records thousands of small sales and must save each one immediately and reliably is an OLTP workload. OLTP handles high volumes of small, fast transactions with ACID guarantees. OLAP, batch and stream analytics are for analysis.

scenario: In a relational table of customers, which column property guarantees that each row can be uniquely identified?

options.note: A foreign key references another table's key; values can repeat.
An index speeds lookups but doesn't guarantee uniqueness.
It supplies a value when none is given; it doesn't enforce uniqueness.

explanation: A primary key uniquely identifies every row in a table and can't be null. A foreign key only references another table's key, and a non-unique index or default constraint doesn't guarantee uniqueness.

scenario: A global app needs a NoSQL database with single-digit-millisecond reads and writes in several Azure regions and a choice of APIs such as NoSQL, MongoDB and Cassandra. Which service should you choose?

options.note: It's a relational database, not a multi-API NoSQL service.
It's a managed relational MySQL service.
It's a managed relational PostgreSQL service.

explanation: Azure Cosmos DB is a globally distributed NoSQL database with single-digit millisecond latency and multi-region writes. It offers several APIs including NoSQL, MongoDB and Cassandra. Azure SQL Database, MySQL and PostgreSQL are relational services.

scenario: In a Power BI report, which visual is best for showing how monthly revenue changed over the past two years?

options.note: Pie charts show parts of a whole at one point in time.
A card shows a single value.
Scatter charts show the relationship between two measures.

explanation: A line chart shows a measure across a continuous time axis, which makes a trend such as monthly revenue over two years easy to see. A pie chart shows proportions of a whole, a card shows one value and a scatter chart shows correlation.

scenario: Data is copied from source systems, cleaned and reshaped in a separate engine, and then loaded into a data warehouse. What is this process called?

options.note: In ELT the data is loaded first and transformed inside the target store.

explanation: In ETL the data is extracted, transformed (cleaned and reshaped) in a separate engine, and then loaded into the warehouse. In ELT the raw data is loaded first and transformed inside the destination.
